items.title: Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1969-12-14
items.q: I hate to call anything jazz anymore, because everything south of Beethoven has been called jazz

ctx.x: Yeah, that was 50 when you went to St. Charles. So it was around 50, and that was a W.C. Handy tune, incidentally. Yeah. Who is, well, was around Memphis, wasn't born there, also around Mississippi, where he heard those real blues. And he heard the real folk musicians, you might say, playing with the homemade instruments, and picked up on this idea. I think it's marvelous that Handy collected these things and rearranged them before they were lost to the world. He was an educated man, as a matter of fact, a music…

Well, I tell you, I hate to call anything jazz anymore, because everything south of Beethoven has been called jazz, and I don't know what jazz is and what jazz isn't. I know the kind of musicians that I like to play with, and they call that jazz, and that's the best I can do with that.
Uh-huh. Well, the reason I'm asking, I have a record, and it has a picture on it, like a painting on the record. Would that be worth anything? It's made by the Vogue Record Company.
